currentContext.business: Digitide helps enterprises reimagine their operations through AI-led innovation, deep domain expertise and global delivery, solving business problems across banking, financial services, insurance, healthcare, manufacturing, retail and e-commerce. It blends onshore consulting and advisory with offshore engineering and operations, running two service lines - Tech & Digital Services (AI engineering, data and analytics, cloud, enterprise platform solutions) and BPM/BPaaS Services (AI-augmented processes, platform-led automation, outcome-linked delivery). currentContext.strategies: The '3X Strategy' growth framework - a Growth vector (unifying the global workforce under 'One Digitide', building differentiated talent, industrialising the international sales engine with dedicated farming and hunting motions, executing large deals, and an ecosystem of hyperscaler / SI / platform partnerships, with targeted inorganic growth in adjacent markets and verticals as an active lever).|Core Verticals: high-conviction vertical bets - internationally on Insurance and Banking, Healthcare and Fast Growth Tech (FGT); domestically on Insurance and Banking, Manufacturing and Automotive, and FGT - selected on structural tailwinds, demonstrated domain depth and platform scalability.|Service Lines: scaling two primary service lines - Tech & Digital Services (AI engineering, data and analytics, cloud, enterprise platform solutions) and BPM/BPaaS Services (AI-augmented processes, platform-led automation, outcome-linked delivery for margin accretion).|'One Digitide' unification - aggregating business divisions, aligning teams around shared client accounts and rationalising the operating footprint (premises and delivery locations) so the organisation answers to client outcomes rather than internal silos.|Move 1 - shift to an 'interlock' operating model where the account is the primary currency: service lines, geographies and functions lock arms around each client with one view of the account and one growth plan.|Move 2 - modernise the India-market core (contact centre operations, transactional processing, payroll and collections) with new thinking, new technology and new talent rather than treating it as legacy.|Move 3 - 'Go west, go digital' as a challenger in international markets, with Tech & Digital remaining the focus and investment area, purposed on delivering client business outcomes.|Move 4 - fill the white space deliberately: organic build where there is time and talent, partnerships where speed matters, acquisitions where fit and timing are right.|AI at the core, not bolted on - redesigning workflows, delivery models and commercial models so AI does more of the heavy lifting and people move up the value chain; increasingly selling and pricing value delivered rather than effort expended.|Deliberate transition from effort-based to outcome-linked commercial models: multi-year managed-services retainers, AI Innovation-as-a-Service subscriptions, outcome-based pricing tied to productivity/automation/operational KPIs, and a Value Management Office (VMO) embedding value realisation from programme design with KPI-linked OKRs, gain-share pricing and board-level AI ROI reporting.|AI-led differentiation and responsible-AI governance as a moat: continued investment in proprietary platforms and the Pulse.ai ecosystem, plus embedded ethical AI principles (bias-free design, explainability, human-in-the-loop oversight, adversarial resilience, audit logging).|Portfolio diversification across geographies, verticals, client segments and service lines to mitigate concentration and cyclicality risk; currentContext.expansion: Digitide is an asset-light services business - the annual report describes footprint and delivery capacity, not plant capacity. Expansion in FY26 was organisational and geographic rather than physical: under the 'One Digitide' unification the Company rationalised its operating footprint, 'including changes in premises and delivery locations', while aggregating business divisions and aligning teams around shared client accounts (Chairman's message). The delivery base is more than 40 locations across 5 countries with around 53,500 professionals and 40 global delivery centres, and the model is explicitly built on 'privileged access to talent across India's Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities' (the 40-locations/5-countries and 40-delivery-centre statements sit in the Corporate Overview and MD&A text routed to the profile and strategy_outlook bundles - the Corporate Overview extract in this capex bundle is head-truncated and starts mid-word at 'arkets.'). Geographic expansion is focused on the United States and Canada, supported by deliberate investment in global sales capability. New-entity expansion: Digitide IT Solutions L.L.C was incorporated as a wholly-owned subsidiary on 11 March 2026, and the Company states it 'is in the process of making investment in its subsidiary', with no operations in that subsidiary till 31 March 2026 (back-filled from Form AOC-1, which was routed to the profile and governance_entities bundles, not to this one). Inorganic capacity addition remains an explicit lever - 'acquisitions where fit and timing are right' and 'targeted inorganic growth through acquisitions in adjacent markets and verticals'. Platform build-out (Pulse.ai ecosystem, Pulse.nerve, Insurance.ai, DigiCollect 2.0, SWIFTclose) is the Company's substitute for physical capex. NOTE ON SOURCES: the MD&A text routed under this bundle's MD&A heading is entirely industry/macro commentary (global IT-BPM sizing, NASSCOM/Gartner/IMF data, India data-centre and GCC statistics) and contains no company capex narrative; the India data-centre doubling by 2027 and the Rs 20,000 M Union Budget FY26 AI allocation are industry facts about India, not Digitide commitments.

risks.note: Digitide faces competition from large multinational IT-BPM firms, agile digital-native disruptors and hyperscaler ecosystems, all intensifying pressure on market share and pricing (MD&A, Challenges and Risks).

risks.risk: AI-led disruption of traditional service delivery models
risks.note: While AI fuels growth it also accelerates disruption of traditional delivery, necessitating continuous reskilling and workforce evolution; AI-led automation may moderate traditional headcount-driven BPM growth, and outcome-linked pricing forces a rethink of how work is priced as AI reduces manual effort - a structural threat to the ~70% of revenue that is BPM-weighted.

Global data protection regulations including GDPR and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, alongside emerging AI governance frameworks (EU AI Act, sector-specific AI rules in financial services and healthcare), introduce increasing compliance burdens in cross-border engagements.

Shortages in high-demand areas such as AI engineering, cloud architecture and cybersecurity continue to drive hiring costs and attrition, particularly in North America; AI-ready skills are in limited supply industry-wide.

Inflationary pressure, recession concerns, trade policy changes and evolving visa and immigration regulations may delay client decision cycles or constrain outsourcing budgets; the MD&A also cites Gartner's 'uncertainty pause' in discretionary, project-based technology spending and IMF risks tilted to the downside for 2026-27.

Heightened frequency and sophistication of cyberattacks require continuous investment in security infrastructure, compliance and operational resilience; mitigation cited includes advanced threat detection, AI risk validation, red-team adversarial testing, role-based access control and PII detection.

Structural concentration despite improvement: top 30 customers contributed 58.1% of FY26 revenue, top 20 49.3% and top 10 35.8% (versus 61.2%/52.2%/37.9% in FY25). [Provenance: Corporate Overview concentration disclosure, routed to the profile / capex_expansion / registry bundles - no concentration data was routed into risks_esg.]

BFSI remains the largest vertical at 52% of FY26 revenue, and 62.7% of revenue is domestic with 37.3% international, so a BFSI spending pause or an India demand shock transmits directly. [Provenance: Corporate Overview revenue-mix commentary in the profile / capex_expansion bundles.]

risks.risk: Transition and integration risk from the demerger
risks.note: FY26 was the first year of independent operations following the Composite Scheme of Arrangement with Quess Corp and Bluspring: the Company had to build standalone corporate functions, navigate contract novations, regulatory realignment and balance-sheet restructuring, and absorbed demerger-related exceptional costs - execution risk that management flags explicitly, alongside DSO peaking during the Q1 contract-novation phase.

CEO change during/after the year - Gurmeet Singh Chahal (ED & CEO w.e.f. 01 April 2025) hands over to Sameer Ahluwalia, who 'takes the helm this June', at the same moment the Company is shifting from capability-building to execution at scale.

The MD&A cites industry-wide concerns around automation-led pricing pressure, slower deal cycles and uncertainty over AI monetisation models prompting a broader reassessment of growth visibility, with providers pressured to demonstrate AI outcomes rather than AI investment; McKinsey data cited shows more than 80% of respondents not yet seeing tangible EBIT impact from GenAI.

one-line thesis: Digitide successfully pivoted to an AI-first model with Tech & Digital revenue growing 27.2% YoY, offsetting BPM stagnation, though FY26 profitability was suppressed by one-time wage code charges and demerger costs. The path to FY31's $1Bn target relies on accelerating international mix (now 38%) and converting hyperscaler partnerships into large-scale enterprise deals.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Digitide helps enterprises reimagine their operations through AI-led innovation, deep domain expertise and global delivery, solving business problems across banking, financial services, insurance, healthcare, manufacturing, retail and e-commerce. It blends onshore consulting and advisory with offshore engineering and operations, running two service lines - Tech & Digital Services (AI engineering, data and analytics, cloud, enterprise platform solutions) and BPM/BPaaS Services (AI-augmented processes, platform-led automation, outcome-linked delivery). Around 53,500 professionals serve more than 300 clients worldwide from over 40 locations across 5 countries, headquartered in Bengaluru; the group includes Alldigi Tech, its international Customer Lifecycle Management and Payroll business.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Enterprise AI moving from adoption to industrialisation - management argues the differentiator is no longer access to AI but the ability to engineer AI into core workflows, which shifts demand toward partners who can combine AI engineering, domain expertise and operational integration.
- Accelerating adoption of Agentic AI, GenAI and intelligent automation across BFSI, healthcare, manufacturing and technology verticals creating demand for end-to-end AI engineering, deployment and governance - areas where the Company says it holds differentiated proprietary assets.
- Platform-led managed services demand: the addressable AI services market for IT firms is expected to nearly double by 2028 as enterprises prefer integrated outcome-driven partnerships over point solutions.
- Cloud and infrastructure modernization - continued migration to cloud-native architectures, HPC and sovereign cloud driving demand for multi-vendor orchestration and infrastructure management.
- BPM market growth: the Indian BPM market is projected to grow at 5-6% annually while North America, a key market for Digitide, is expected to grow at 7-8%, driven by higher-value outsourcing and enterprise AI investment.
- SMB digitalization expanding the addressable base for platform-led, bundled 'as-a-service' offerings.
- Fortune 500 enterprises seeking trusted transformation partners with demonstrated AI depth, supporting deeper and new strategic client relationships.
- Vertical tailwinds: BFSI (AI-driven automation, real-time fraud detection, digital banking platforms, regulatory compliance), Healthcare (AI-powered patient engagement, telehealth, claims and revenue-cycle automation), Manufacturing & Automotive (Industry 4.0, supply-chain intelligence, predictive maintenance, ESG compliance) and Fast Growth Tech (hyper-personalisation, AI-driven engagement, digital financial services).
- North American Tech & Digital services market remains resilient with cloud infrastructure services attracting enterprise investment; GenAI expected to reshape IT services particularly in knowledge management and contact centre augmentation.
- Commercial-model shift toward BPaaS, outcome-based pricing and risk-sharing as AI reduces the manual effort embedded in traditional delivery - a structural change in how services are priced and delivered.
- Own platform proof points cited as demand drivers: DigiCollect 2.0 demonstrating live recovery improvements, DigiSaiL targeting a step-change in lead conversion economics, Pulse.nerve redefining enterprise AI orchestration and AI Innovation-as-a-Service enabling clients to move from pilots to production-scale AI.
- Client relationships many spanning over a decade, and a talent base of 53,500 professionals across 40 global delivery centres, described as the most enduring competitive advantage.
- TCV bookings of Rs 23,550 M during FY26, alongside the addition of 114 new client logos - described as evidence of a stronger commercial engine (CEO letter and Corporate Overview).
- 'Our commercial engine remained strong through the year, reflected in a healthy deal pipeline and continued client additions' (Chairman's message).
- 'We enter FY27 with a stronger pipeline, a more integrated operating model, and a leadership team aligned on execution' (Chairman's message).
- 'We enter FY27 with a record pipeline, a strengthened balance ...' - the CEO's closing pipeline statement is cut off mid-sentence at the end of the routed Chairman/CEO section, so the full claim could not be captured.
- An active pilot programme for the SWIFTclose (Sales.ai) platform across 20 enterprise accounts, being commercialised as a SaaS product with outcome-based pricing (this sentence is head-truncated in the strategy_outlook bundle - full text back-filled from the risks_esg bundle, MD&A 'Platform Monetization and AI Deal Models').

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Digitide is an asset-light services business - the annual report describes footprint and delivery capacity, not plant capacity. Expansion in FY26 was organisational and geographic rather than physical: under the 'One Digitide' unification the Company rationalised its operating footprint, 'including changes in premises and delivery locations', while aggregating business divisions and aligning teams around shared client accounts (Chairman's message). The delivery base is more than 40 locations across 5 countries with around 53,500 professionals and 40 global delivery centres, and the model is explicitly built on 'privileged access to talent across India's Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities' (the 40-locations/5-countries and 40-delivery-centre statements sit in the Corporate Overview and MD&A text routed to the profile and strategy_outlook bundles - the Corporate Overview extract in this capex bundle is head-truncated and starts mid-word at 'arkets.'). Geographic expansion is focused on the United States and Canada, supported by deliberate investment in global sales capability. New-entity expansion: Digitide IT Solutions L.L.C was incorporated as a wholly-owned subsidiary on 11 March 2026, and the Company states it 'is in the process of making investment in its subsidiary', with no operations in that subsidiary till 31 March 2026 (back-filled from Form AOC-1, which was routed to the profile and governance_entities bundles, not to this one). Inorganic capacity addition remains an explicit lever - 'acquisitions where fit and timing are right' and 'targeted inorganic growth through acquisitions in adjacent markets and verticals'. Platform build-out (Pulse.ai ecosystem, Pulse.nerve, Insurance.ai, DigiCollect 2.0, SWIFTclose) is the Company's substitute for physical capex. NOTE ON SOURCES: the MD&A text routed under this bundle's MD&A heading is entirely industry/macro commentary (global IT-BPM sizing, NASSCOM/Gartner/IMF data, India data-centre and GCC statistics) and contains no company capex narrative; the India data-centre doubling by 2027 and the Rs 20,000 M Union Budget FY26 AI allocation are industry facts about India, not Digitide commitments.

- Customer recognition - Premier Partner under CARE, Axis Bank's Partner Loyalty Programme; winner at the Google Cloud Gen AI Exchange Hackathon 2025
